summary: Calculates the Bare Soil Index (BSI) from Sentinel-2 data.
description:
The Bare Soil Index (BSI) process uses Sentinel-2 imagery to identify patches of land that are bare (exposed soil) versus those covered by vegetation. It works by combining four different bands of light captured by the satellite: blue (B02), red (B04), near-infrared (B08), and shortwave infrared (B11), using the formula: 
 $$BSI = ((B11 + B04) - (B02 + B08)) / ((B11 + B04) + (B02 + B08))$$. Bare soil and vegetation reflect these different wavelengths of light in distinct ways, healthy plants strongly reflect near-infrared light and absorb red and blue light, while bare soil reflects red and shortwave infrared light more evenly and lacks the strong near-infrared signature of plants. By comparing the combined red and shortwave-infrared signal against the combined blue and near-infrared signal, and then scaling the result so it always falls between -1 and 1, BSI produces a value that is easy to compare across different fields, dates, and lighting conditions. In general, higher (more positive) BSI values indicate bare or exposed soil, such as freshly plowed fields, fallow land, or areas with sparse crop cover, while lower (more negative) values indicate healthy, dense vegetation. This makes BSI especially useful in agriculture for monitoring field conditions, tracking planting and harvest cycles, detecting soil erosion, or identifying areas that may need attention before the next growing season.

parameters.name: spatial_extent
parameters.description:
Limits the data to process to the specified bounding box or polygons.

For raster data, the process loads the pixel into the data cube if the point at the pixel center intersects with the bounding box or any of the polygons (as defined in the Simple Features standard by the OGC).
For vector data, the process loads the geometry into the data cube if the geometry is fully within the bounding box or any of the polygons (as defined in the Simple Features standard by the OGC). Empty geometries may only be in the data cube if no spatial extent has been provided.

Empty geometries are ignored.
Set this parameter to null to set no limit for the spatial extent.

base.description: Base (optional, lower left corner, coordinate axis 3).

height.description: Height (optional, upper right corner, coordinate axis 3).

crs.description: Coordinate reference system of the extent, specified as as [EPSG code](http://www.epsg-registry.org/) or [WKT2 CRS string](http://docs.opengeospatial.org/is/18-010r7/18-010r7.html). Defaults to `4326` (EPSG code 4326) unless the client explicitly requests a different coordinate reference system.

schema.title: Vector data cube
schema.description: Limits the data cube to the bounding box of the given geometries in the vector data cube. For raster data, all pixels inside the bounding box that do not intersect with any of the polygons will be set to no data (`null`). Empty geometries are ignored.

schema.title: No filter
schema.description: Don't filter spatially. All data is included in the data cube.

parameters.name: temporal_extent
parameters.description: Temporal extent specified as two-element array with start and end date/date-time.
